features.title: Real ECGs, explained

home.privacy_line: Your progress stays in this browser. We ask for no account, email or other personal data.
home.who_heading: For anyone who reads ECGs on call, on the ward or in the ambulance

faq.a: Nothing. The ECG trainer and the ECG of the week are free and need no account.

faq.q: What data do you keep about me?
faq.a: None. There are no forms and no accounts. Your progress in the trainer is saved only in your browser, and you can clear it at any time.

faq.q: Can I send you my own ECG or a patient's?
faq.a: No. The content is for education only and doesn't replace medical care. For a real ECG, please see your own doctor.

faq.q: I found a mistake. Who do I tell?
faq.a: Email us at {email} with the case code shown in the trainer. We fix things quickly.

home.steps_heading: Read every ECG in the same order
home.steps_intro: The trainer builds the habit of a systematic read: the same steps, in the same order, on every tracing.
steps: Sinus or not? Regular or irregular?
How many complexes a minute? Slow, normal or fast.
Are there P waves? Is each followed by a QRS? Is the PR normal, short or long?
Narrow or wide? Bundle branch block, hypertrophy, Q waves?
ST elevation or depression, inverted T waves, reciprocal changes.
All of it in one line, as in the notes.
